gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-gujarat: Amadeus stretches its words wide across the line, round letters bent from a single wire. Noto Serif Gujarati reads in a bookish, authoritative voice, its oversized counters keeping long paragraphs easy going.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-kannada: Noto Serif Kannada reads traditional and literary, its big counters and middle-of-the-road stroke contrast giving each line a familiar texture. Amadeus sprawls and commands; Noto Serif Kannada quietly carries the text.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-khmer: Wide, wiry and unapologetic: that is Amadeus up top. Noto Serif Khmer arrives with lighter horizontals that never turn threadlike, giving the blueprint-style headline a classic, authoritative footing underneath.
gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Pilcrow Rounded packs its letters tightly, tall in the lowercase, with curves that refuse to shut. Pilcrow Rounded is the warm one, built for steady text, while Arkhip floats its geometric letters apart and shows off.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-arvo: Modern and geometric, Arkhip floats its letters apart, each stroke held at one fixed pressure. And Arvo, traditional and dignified, does the quieter job of carrying text, its curves refusing to close.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-belgrano: Belgrano brings a classic, traditional feel, with open-mouthed curves that stay clear and a low lowercase beneath Arkhip's single-thickness lines. The standout is Arkhip's single-weight strokes against Belgrano's serifs.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-enriqueta: Sleek and spaced out up top: Arkhip glides under the eye like wire, while Enriqueta's chalky curves stop short of closing. Nudge Enriqueta's size up a notch, since its lowercase runs low.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-gowun-batang: Crisp, single-weight lines up top: Arkhip's skeleton never thickens or thins. Gowun Batang cuts its terminals back to leave a big gap, giving that rigid skeleton a refined, literary counterpoint.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-habibi: Sleek and spaced out: Arkhip's stems match its hairlines because there are none, and its letters float apart. Habibi's editorial serif sits beneath, giving each headline a traditional anchor.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-inika: One constant stroke width runs through every Arkhip letter, floating them well apart. And Inika, classic and traditional, keeps a low lowercase and an s you can see through.
